blocks.headline: Report: Student Wins Prize for Clear Presentation
paras: Final-year student Rui Matos won the university’s presentation prize on Friday with a talk on water scarcity. He **opened with a question**: “How much water did you use this morning?” Then he gave a **roadmap**: “I will make three points.”

Judges praised his **signposting** (“**Turning to** my second point…”), his **simple slides** and his **final call to action**. “**To conclude**, small habits change big systems,” he said, before **inviting questions**.

items.why: signposting = sinalizar a estrutura do discurso.

blocks.body: Uma boa apresentação **diz o que vai dizer, diz, e diz o que disse**. Use **sinalização**: *Let me begin with…, Turning to…, To conclude…*
Slides cheios de texto distraem: leia menos do slide e fale mais.

items.s: ___ to my second point, let me show a chart. (Turning)
To ___ , small habits change big systems. (conclude)

body: **Let me begin by…** — Deixe-me começar…
**Turning to…** — Passando a…
**As you can see from this slide,…** — Como vocês veem neste slide,…
**That brings me to…** — Isso me leva a…
**To conclude,…** — Para concluir,…
**I’d be happy to take questions.** — Terei prazer em responder perguntas.
**Let me stress that…** — Deixe-me enfatizar que…
**Break the ice with…** — Quebrar o gelo com…
**How do you open your talk?** — Como você abre sua apresentação?
**With a question, then a roadmap.** — Com uma pergunta, depois um roteiro.
**And during the talk?** — E durante a fala?

To conclude, small habits change big systems. Any questions?

blocks.task: Write the script for the first 6 sentences of a presentation on a topic of your choice: hook, roadmap, point one.
blocks.model: Good morning. How many hours did you sleep last night? Today I will make three points: why sleep matters, what disturbs it, and how to improve it. Let me begin with the first point. Studies associate poor sleep with weak memory. That is why schools should start later.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
